gaps_found.description: No session counter tracking mechanism exists. The deep audit triggers at 'session counter mod 20 = 0' but there is no repository-level session counter. Session numbers are assigned ad-hoc in file names and report headers — there is no central SESSION_COUNTER.md, no monotonic increment guarantee, and no mechanism to detect when the counter should tick. Without a counter, the mod-20 trigger cannot fire autonomously — it requires human or autonomous agent awareness to recognize the threshold.
gaps_found.framework_reference: M3 trigger_event: 'Session counter mod 20 = 0'; M3 cadence frequency: 'Every 20 sessions'
gaps_found.recommendation: Create a SESSION_COUNTER.md file (or embed in CURRENT_BASELINES.md) that: (a) stores the most recent session number, (b) is incremented at every session start by the Governance Auditor during T0 entry, (c) is referenced by the Deep Audit trigger check (T0-CHK-6 proposed: 'Check session counter mod 20. If 0, queue Deep Audit for this session').

gaps_found.description: G1 cross-references MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md as an independent count source, but that file is generated from source files (governance-guard Rule 3). If re-generated at each Deep Audit, it will always match the parse-count, removing its value as an independent verification for G1. This is the same tautology issue as S3-GAP-2.

G5 requires cross-referencing against 'known-defective QID list from DEFECT_LIBRARY.md' but the DEFECT_LIBRARY.md does not maintain a consolidated, machine-parseable defective QID list. Each defect entry lists affected QIDs in prose/table form. Extracting the full defective QID list from DEFECT_LIBRARY.md is a manual, error-prone process. For a 60-90 minute Deep Audit with parallel agents, this is a bottleneck.
gaps_found.recommendation: Add to M5_BASELINE_REFRESH: generate a machine-parseable DEFECTIVE_QID_LIST.json (QID → DL-ID → severity → status) from DEFECT_LIBRARY.md entries. Update during each baseline refresh. Use this as the authoritative cross-reference for G5 and PD-CHK-2, not raw DEFECT_LIBRARY.md parsing.

At domain closure? At the next 20-session boundary? Both?
gaps_found.framework_reference: M3 trigger_event: 'Session counter mod 20 = 0, OR achievement of a domain-closure milestone'
gaps_found.recommendation: Clarify: 'Domain-closure milestones trigger an immediate Deep Audit regardless of session counter. The session counter resets to 0 after a milestone-triggered Deep Audit, starting a new 20-session cycle.'

cross_cutting_gaps.title: No Inter-Agent Communication Protocol
cross_cutting_gaps.description: Multiple escalation procedures require broadcasts ('halt all agents', 'notify all pack-write agents') but the framework provides no concrete mechanism for inter-agent communication. The notification_chain fields describe WHO should be notified but not HOW. In practice, agents operate in isolated contexts; a 'halt broadcast' requires a coordination mechanism (shared state file, session-level flag, or convention) that does not exist in the current architecture.
framework_references: ESC-001 notification_chain: 'Discovering agent → Remediation Agent → Governance Auditor → All pack-write agents (halt broadcast)'
ESC-005 notification_chain: 'Discovering agent → Governance Auditor → All agents (halt broadcast)'
ESC-006 notification_chain: 'Discovering agent → Governance Auditor → All agents (halt broadcast)'
cross_cutting_gaps.recommendation: Three-tier approach: (1) IMMEDIATE — adopt convention that all pack-write agents MUST run governance guard (Rule 2 check) before every write batch. If the guard fails with a halt flag, writes are blocked. No broadcast needed — the guard is the gate. (2) SHORT-TERM — create a HALT_FLAG.md file in the repo root that the Governance Auditor writes to when a halt is declared. All agents check for this file before write operations. (3) MEDIUM-TERM — implement a session-level halt flag in CURRENT_BASELINES.md §6 (runtime status section).

cross_cutting_gaps.title: Baseline Data Integrity Dependency
cross_cutting_gaps.description: Multiple T0 checks and Deep Audit gates validate against CURRENT_BASELINES.md, which is documented as stale (GAP-005/GAP-6: phantom DL-008 items in §3; S724 operational readiness score 23/25 due to two documentation gaps). This means T0-CHK-1 (hash verification), T0-CHK-3 (DL-008 count), DA-CHK-4 (G4 baseline hash stability), and DA-CHK-5 (G5 delivery pool safety) may all produce PASS results against incorrect reference data. The framework is structurally valid but operationally compromised until the baseline data is corrected.
cross_cutting_gaps.recommendation: P0 priority: execute S726 as prescribed (governance guard upgrade + CURRENT_BASELINES.md §3 refresh). Until GAP-004 and GAP-005 are closed, all T0 and Deep Audit results should carry a 'BASELINE_INTEGRITY_CAVEAT' flag noting that reference data may be stale.

cross_cutting_gaps.title: May Coaching Layer Runtime Dependency Without Ownership
cross_cutting_gaps.description: Three separate operational paths reference the May coaching layer: (1) T-002 quarantine step references May's DEFECT_MANIFEST, (2) PD-CHK-2 cross-references May's DEFECT_MANIFEST_DL008_DL026.json, (3) T0-CHK-1 verifies may-core.js and may-learner-state.js hashes. All three reference a component whose ownership is GAP-1 (unassigned). Until GAP-1 is resolved, these checks have an orphaned dependency.
framework_references: T-002 prescribed_actions item 2: 'add to May's DEFECT_MANIFEST if coaching layer active'
PD-CHK-2 description: 'Also cross-reference May's DEFECT_MANIFEST_DL008_DL026.json if coaching layer active'
cross_cutting_gaps.recommendation: Resolve GAP-1 as prescribed (assign to 100-series Maintenance Agent). Until resolved, all May-layer-dependent checks should fall back to DEFECT_LIBRARY.md as the authoritative defective QID source.

cross_cutting_gaps.title: No Automated T0 Execution Script
cross_cutting_gaps.description: The T0 protocol requires ~5 minutes of manual agent commands (PowerShell hash computation, grep counts, Function constructor parse, governance guard test execution). GAP-006 identifies this and recommends scripts/t0_baseline_verify.js. Without automation, human error, protocol drift, or session-start rush can cause missed checks. This is especially critical in maintenance mode where 'Every session start' requires T0 completion.
cross_cutting_gaps.recommendation: Create scripts/t0_baseline_verify.js as a single-command T0 executor that: (a) runs all 5 checks, (b) outputs pass/fail per check with evidence, (c) captures summary to REVISION_HISTORY.md format, (d) returns exit code 0 (all pass) or 1 (any fail). This eliminates manual protocol drift.

readiness_caveats: Framework structure and escalation logic are complete and internally consistent across all 6 simulated scenarios. All triggers fire correctly, escalation paths are traceable from detection to clearance, and ownership assignments are clear for every cadence and threshold.

Operational readiness is compromised by known baseline data integrity issues (GAP-004, GAP-005, GAP-006) and the unassigned May coaching layer ownership (GAP-1). These do not block maintenance mode conceptually but they DO block full operational activation — the 23/25 readiness score from S724 is accurate.

The inter-agent communication protocol (X-GAP-1) is the most significant implementation gap. The governance convention that 'all agents check governance guard before writes' is the recommended bridging mechanism until a formal halt protocol is implemented.

All 6 scenarios received PASS verdicts because the framework logic is correct — the gaps are in operational implementation, not structural design. The framework would function as designed IF: (a) baselines are corrected, (b) May layer ownership is assigned, and (c) inter-agent halt convention is adopted.
framework_revision_rationale: No structural revision required. The S723 framework and S725 trigger registry are complete and internally consistent. The 13 gaps identified (6 per-scenario + 4 cross-cutting + 3 from prior S724 assessment) are operational implementation gaps, not framework design defects. They should be addressed through the prescribed remediation sessions (S726 for GAP-004/005/006, S310 for Deep Audit, 800-series for certification pipeline) rather than through framework revision.
